Actually, any shooter you like. If you want different music it's worth pointing out that every game ever lets you turn off the in game music without disabling the rest of the game's sound in the audio menu.

If you're on PC, turn off the music and run a music player with your preferred playlist in the background. I do this all the time, I just recently finished Just Cause 3 and played 90% of the game that way. Steam has an integrated audio player that lets you do this, but you can use any desktop music player and it works. I like using the Steam Music player or Foobar 2000 for this myself.

You can do the same with many console games, but might not be able to play music from the console itself depending on the system and game. Not everyone installs music on their console and it can be a pain to get some music files to play because of DRM even if they are perfectly legal digital music. Putting on some music on a separate stereo works almost as well though. If your stereo is also the audio out for your console, you can always set it up so the console audio outputs using the TV speakers and play music using your sound system while you play.
